title: Fix: add ALTER TABLE migration for recipes.slug + drink_recipes.slug
description:
## Why
Production deploy on dietpi is broken: \"no such column: recipes.slug\" / \"no such column: drink_recipes.slug\" from every recipe-listing query.

## Root cause
Commit 9d46bed (\"refactor: simplify slugs to pre-release form\") added the \`slug\` column to \`recipes\` and \`drink_recipes\` by editing the existing \`m20260118_000002_create_recipes\` and \`m20260213_000010_create_drink_recipes\` migrations IN-PLACE, rather than adding a new ALTER TABLE migration. SeaORM tracks already-run migrations by name, so existing DBs (like dietpi's) skip the modified migrations and never gain the column. New code queries the missing column and 500s.

## What's needed
New migration \`m20260424_000012_add_recipe_slugs\`:
1. \`ALTER TABLE recipes ADD COLUMN slug TEXT\` (nullable initially)
2. \`ALTER TABLE drink_recipes ADD COLUMN slug TEXT\` (nullable initially)
3. Backfill: iterate existing rows, compute \`slugify(name)\`, dedupe collisions by appending \`-2\`, \`-3\`, etc., write back
4. Create unique indexes \`idx_recipes_slug\` and \`idx_drink_recipes_slug\`
5. Skip the NOT NULL upgrade — SQLite would require the create-copy-drop-rename dance, and the app always populates slug. Existing fresh DBs already have NOT NULL; this drift is acceptable.

## Verification
- \`cargo test\` green
- Migration applies cleanly on a snapshot of the pre-slug schema
- Migration is no-op on a fresh DB (column already exists from the edited create migration — guard with a column-exists check, or use \`if not exists\` on the indexes)
- Deploy to dietpi via \`just deploy dietpi@dietpi.local\`, verify Recipes tab loads
close_reason: Implemented as new migration m20260424_000012_backfill_recipe_slugs. Idempotent across legacy + fresh DBs via has_column gate. Tests cover backfill, collision dedup, fallback, idempotency, uniqueness. Pushed in 38c01aa. Awaiting deploy verification on dietpi.

title: MCP server rejects non-localhost Host headers — blocks LAN deploy
description:
Connecting to the deployed MCP endpoint at http://dietpi.local:3000/mcp from another machine fails with HTTP 403:

    Forbidden: Host header is not allowed

The rejection comes from rmcp's StreamableHttpService, which ships with a DNS-rebinding-protection allowlist defaulting to ["localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1"] (rmcp-1.4.0 src/transport/streamable_http_server/tower.rs:72). server/src/mcp/mod.rs:100 builds the service with StreamableHttpServerConfig::default(), inheriting that localhost-only allowlist. Any LAN hostname (dietpi.local, IP) gets a 403.

This breaks the README's own LAN-deploy story — the threat model at mcp/mod.rs:18-23 explicitly accepts LAN-side trust, but the host allowlist hadn't been widened to match.

## Fix

Make the allowlist configurable via MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS env var (comma-separated). Merge with — not replace — the rmcp localhost defaults so dev mode never breaks. Empty/unset env var = current behavior.

Tests:
- env var unset → defaults preserved
- env var set with extra hosts → hosts appended, defaults still present
- ports handled per rmcp semantics (entry without port matches any port)

After deploy: set MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS=dietpi.local on the dietpi box's systemd unit / launcher.

## Why P1
Holding up release — without it Claude Desktop can't connect to the deployed server at all.
close_reason: Closed

title: Document MCP threat model: LAN-only, name-is-not-a-credential, any-authed-user-is-admin
description:
The MCP server uses family-member display name as the bearer token (Authorization: Bearer Alice). This is a deliberate 'household trust' design, but the security posture relies entirely on the operator firewalling the port — and that requirement is not documented anywhere reachable by an admin who doesn't read source.

**Three structural facts that need explicit documentation:**

1. /mcp is LAN-only by design. The server binds 0.0.0.0 (server/src/main.rs:64). Operator MUST firewall the port or place behind a reverse proxy with real auth before exposing the host beyond the LAN.

2. Authentication is identity selection, not a secret. Names appear in list_people, get_family_overview, shopping briefs, and meal plans. They are not credentials.

3. Any authenticated family member can read and write any data. There is no per-user authorization. AuthenticatedPerson is plumbed through but only whoami reads it.

**Where to put it:**
- README.md — short note in MCP section
- server/src/mcp/mod.rs — top-of-file doc comment with the same content (so contributors see it before extending the surface)

**Out of scope for this bead:** replacing the auth scheme (tracked separately). Goal here is to make the threat model explicit so the release ships honest about its security posture.
close_reason: Closed

title: Migration: add or_alternative pass-through to frozen Ingredient structs in m13/m14/m15
description:
The three new backfill migrations each redefine an Ingredient struct (per the 'migrations are frozen-in-time' rule in CLAUDE.md). The runtime IngredientDto got an or_alternative field in fewd-4nb, but the frozen migration structs do not.

**Failure mode:** If any of these migrations re-runs against a DB that has or_alternative populated (CI fresh-DB with seeded data, future re-seed scenario, restore-without-seaql_migrations recovery), the field is silently dropped on the JSON round-trip.

**Files:**
- server/migration/src/m20260427_000013_split_ingredient_name_and_prep.rs:78-91
- server/migration/src/m20260428_000014_reparse_misbucketed_ingredients.rs:101-114
- server/migration/src/m20260429_000015_peel_size_parens_from_ingredient_name.rs:79-92

**Fix (trivial, additive):** add to each frozen struct:

```rust
#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
or_alternative: Option<serde_json::Value>,
```

Pass-through Value matches m13's existing pattern for the amount field. Not a re-edit of shipped logic — just a new field added to a struct, which is safe per the migration discipline rules.

Doesn't impact dietpi (migrations already ran there), but blocks any fresh deploy / DB recovery scenario from being safe.
close_reason: Closed

title: Frontend: or_alternative silently dropped in CookingView, AdaptRecipePanel, AiSuggestionSection
description:
Three React components hand-roll their ingredient render and never branch on or_alternative. fewd-9az shipped or_alternative rendering through IngredientLineText, and RecipeDetail/DrinkRecipeDetail/RecipeMatchCard use it correctly. These three bypass it and silently drop the alternative.

**Worst case:** src/components/CookingView.tsx:100-110 — the cooking-time ingredients sidebar. Recipe '8 flour tortillas or 10 corn tortillas' shows only '8 flour tortillas' while the user is cooking.

Other sites (lower severity but same root cause):
- src/components/AdaptRecipePanel.tsx:302-308 (adapted-recipe preview before save)
- src/components/AiSuggestionSection.tsx:409-415 (AI suggestion card)

**Fix:** Replace each inline <li> body with <IngredientLineText ingredient={ing} />. Same swap that's already in place in RecipeDetail, DrinkRecipeDetail, RecipeMatchCard, and the AI results list in CocktailSuggester.

The fewd-9az tests live on IngredientLineText itself, so they don't catch consumers that bypass it. Companion follow-up bead will add integration-level tests asserting or_alternative renders through these three components.

title: Bump vite past path-traversal advisory (5.x → 6.4.2+ or 7.x)
description:
## Why
Open dependabot advisory: \"Vite Vulnerable to Path Traversal in Optimized Deps \`.map\` Handling\" (medium). Vulnerable range is `<= 6.4.1`, so our current vite 5.4.21 is affected. `bun update` cannot move us — package.json pins vite to `^5.0.8` and the fix only exists on later majors.

## What's needed
Major bump with coordinated peer bumps:
- `vite` 5.4.21 → 7.x (latest stable; 6.x is patched at 6.4.2+ but already EOL trajectory)
- `@vitejs/plugin-react` 4.x → 5.x (peer-locked to vite major)
- `vitest` 1.6.x → 3.x (peer-locked to vite major)
- `@vitest/ui` matching vitest major
- Verify `vite.config.ts` and `vitest.config.ts` still compile
- Verify dev server (`bun run dev:full`) still proxies `/api` correctly
- Verify production build + `just deploy` (arm64 build) still works

## Risks
- vite 7 dropped Node 18 support; CI + local dev must be on Node 20+
- vitest 3 has reporter / API changes — some test setup may need tweaks
- jsdom 28 → 29 may be pulled along by vitest peer constraints

## Scope decision
Land as one PR: vite + plugin-react + vitest + ui must move together. Splitting adds churn without isolating risk.

## Verification
- `bun run build` clean
- `bun run test` green (currently 295 pass)
- `bun run lint` clean
- Manual smoke test of dev server + a deploy via `just deploy dietpi@dietpi.local`
close_reason: Closed

title: Remove hardcoded family PII from seed_data.rs
description:
server/src/services/seed_data.rs hardcodes the project owner's family — four first names (Steve, Amanda, Vivienne, Cleo) plus birthdates — into the default seed that runs on first DB init. This was tolerable while the repo was effectively private, but it's now visible in the public repo (and was flagged tangentially by Copilot during PR #9 review of the unrelated bd memory).

The seed is called from db.rs line 17 (seed_if_empty) only when the People table is empty, so changing the values won't disturb existing installs.

Options:
1. Replace the hardcoded list with placeholder/example names ('Alex', 'Jordan', 'Sam', 'Pat') and generic birthdates (e.g. all 1990-01-01). Lowest friction; new installs get a working empty-but-not-empty starter.
2. Drop seed_if_empty entirely so a fresh install presents a real empty state, and rely on the family-add UI to onboard. Cleaner long-term; requires confirming the rest of the app handles a People table with zero rows gracefully (MealPlanner, suggestion flows, etc.).
3. Keep seed for local dev only — gate seed_if_empty behind a SEED_DEMO_DATA env var or debug build cfg.

My recommendation: option 1 for the immediate PII removal, then option 2 as a separate cleanup if/when the empty-state UX is ready.

Acceptance criteria:
- No real names or birthdates in version-controlled seed code.
- Existing installations are unaffected (seed only runs when People is empty).
- A fresh install still produces a usable app (either via placeholder seed or via verified empty-state handling).

Files to touch:
- server/src/services/seed_data.rs (the data)
- Possibly server/src/db.rs (if option 2 or 3)
close_reason: Replaced real family names (Steve/Amanda/Vivienne/Cleo) and birthdates in server/src/services/seed_data.rs with placeholders (Alex/Jordan/Sam/Pat) preserving a 2-adult + 2-child age spread. Updated matching assertion in server/tests/service_tests.rs and the example JSON in REQUIREMENTS.md. Follow-up ticket fewd-esj tracks scrubbing the same names from git history.

title: Recipe enhancer: head-noun matching + honest success signal
description:
The "Enhanced view" toggle on recipe detail (RecipeDetail in src/components/RecipeManager.tsx) shows "Enhanced ✓" but in many recipes nothing actually gets enhanced because the matcher is too strict.

## Root cause

server/src/services/recipe_enhancer.rs:48 — `try_inject` does a literal substring search for the *full* ingredient name (`lower_line.find(&lower_name)`) inside each instruction line. Real recipes write detailed ingredient names ("ripe avocados", "large English cucumber", "kalamata olives", "Greek feta", "dried oregano") but reference the bare head noun in instructions ("avocado", "cucumber", "olives", "feta", "oregano"). Result: zero matches, zero injections, but the request succeeds so the UI lights up the success badge.

Example recipe (from a screenshot reported 2026-05-04): all 5 instruction steps reference ingredients by their bare head noun; not a single ingredient gets injected even though most are clearly referenced.

There's also a latent false-positive bug from the opposite direction: no word boundaries, so "salt" can match "salted water".

## Two decisions to make before implementing

### 1. Matching aggressiveness (pick a stopping point)
- (a) Just plurals: try full name, then trailing `s/es` stripped.
- (b) Plurals + last word: also try the final word ("large English cucumber" → "cucumber"). [Recommended]
- (c) Plurals + last word + modifier stop-word list (large/small/fresh/dried/Greek/kalamata/ripe/Italian/...).

(b) covers the screenshot case without a vocabulary to maintain. Low false-positive risk if anchored on word boundaries.

### 2. Honest success signal
The current "Enhanced ✓" badge fires whenever the request succeeds, even when the enhanced text is identical to the original. Two cheap fixes:
- Frontend-only: compare `enhancedText` to `parsed.instructions` and only badge if they differ.
- Backend: return `{enhanced_text, injection_count}` so the UI can say "3 of 11 ingredients placed" or similar. More informative, helps debug matching gaps in the field.

## Implementation notes
- Keep the full-name attempt as the *primary* match (preserves current safe behavior); only fall back when nothing matched.
- Add word-boundary anchoring to fix the latent "salt"→"salted" false positive.
- Existing tests in server/src/services/recipe_enhancer.rs cover the happy path; add tests for: head-noun fallback, plural handling, "salt vs salted water" non-match, multi-word names where only the head noun appears.
- Frontend touch point: src/components/RecipeManager.tsx around line 1004 (the toggle button + badge).

## Out of scope
- AI/LLM-based ingredient resolution (overkill for this).
- Reworking the ingredient model to carry a separate "canonical name" field (bigger schema change; revisit if (b) proves insufficient).

title: MCP: replace name-bearer auth with per-person opaque tokens
description:
The current MCP auth (Authorization: Bearer <family-member-name>) treats the family member's display name as the credential. Names are low-entropy public-ish identifiers that appear in list_people, get_family_overview, and shopping briefs — anyone who can reach /mcp and guess a name authenticates as them.

This is acceptable on the LAN (per the threat-model docs landing in fewd-2y6.3) but should be replaced with real authentication before the server is ever exposed beyond a firewalled LAN.

**Proposed shape:**
- Issue per-person opaque random token (32+ bytes, base64-url).
- Store hashed at rest (argon2 or bcrypt).
- Compare with subtle::ConstantTimeEq.
- Provision via the web UI (Settings → MCP); display once, then only fingerprint.
- Never log the token.
- Optional: rotation + revocation flow.

**Migration:** new column on person, optional during dev. Once the UI provisioning ships, deprecate name-bearer.

NOT release-gating per the user's explicit decision (LAN-only deployment). File for follow-up release.

title: MCP: cap date-range span and result count in tool validators
description:
DateRangeParams::validate (server/src/mcp/schemas/common.rs:30-55) only rejects malformed dates and reversed ranges. There's no upper bound on the span. start_date=0001-01-01, end_date=9999-12-31 is accepted; the service then loads every meal in the DB, parses every servings JSON blob, and walks MealLookups over the full result. With an LLM driving the tool, a single hallucinated wide range fans out into a multi-megabyte response.

**Affected tools:** list_meals, get_shopping_list (date-range), and list_curated_recipes / search_recipes / list_people (no pagination at all — bounded only by household scale, easy to break with imported public-recipe corpora).

**Fix:** Cap date-range span (e.g. ≤366 days) and result count (e.g. ≤500) in the validator. Return a tool-level error pointing the LLM at a narrower call.

NOT release-gating — household scale is small enough today that this is a theoretical concern. File for follow-up.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #36 (merge 1811d0e). Two caps applied: (1) MAX_DATE_RANGE_DAYS=366 in DateRangeParams::validate via new InputError::DateRangeTooWide variant — protects list_meals and get_shopping_list. (2) MAX_LIST_RESULTS=500 via enforce_list_cap helper — applied to list_curated_recipes, search_recipes, list_people, list_meals, AND get_family_overview (added in Copilot review response abac260 — closes the LLM-bypass that calling get_family_overview instead of list_people would have presented). read_resource for fewd://family/overview intentionally exempt: per MCP 2025-11-25 spec, resources are application-controlled (user attachment), not LLM-addressable autonomously, so the bypass vector doesn't apply. Tests: 6 new (boundary coverage, helper unit, wiring); 88 mcp tests total pass.

title: MCP: redact raw DbErr from db_error()/internal_error() responses
description:
server/src/mcp/handler.rs:471-479 — db_error() and internal_error() format the raw SeaORM Err Display into the JSON-RPC McpError::internal_error response. SeaORM's DbErr embeds the underlying SQLite/SQLx error including column names, constraint names, and sometimes parameter values. A malformed input that triggers a constraint violation will leak schema details to whichever MCP client is talking to the server.

internal_error() has the same shape — formats arbitrary internal messages onto the wire.

**Fix:** Log the verbose detail server-side via tracing. Return a stable opaque message to the client (e.g., 'database error' + a request-id correlation token). Reserve the verbose strings for tool_user_error cases where they're intended to guide an LLM-controlled retry, not for protocol-level errors.

NOT release-gating — the LAN-only deployment posture limits exposure. File for follow-up cleanup.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #35 (merge 8e497053). Wire payload of db_error(), internal_error(), and tool_json_result()'s serialize-failure path now opaque ('database error', 'internal server error', 'failed to serialize result'); verbose detail kept in tracing only. tool_user_error() left verbose intentionally (LLM-actionable retry hints). Refactor: DislikeResolveError::Internal carries String diagnostic; protocol-layer call site wraps via internal_error(). authenticated_name() also picked up tracing in same PR (Copilot review).

title: Surface rmcp parameter-deserialize failures as tool-level errors via LenientParameters<T>
description:
## Why fewd-m95 swept McpError::invalid_params → tool_user_error inside #[tool] handlers, but ONE category of LLM-recoverable failure still emits JSON-RPC -32602 (rendered as opaque "Tool execution failed" in Claude Desktop): rmcp's parameter deserialization happens in the Parameters FromContextPart impl, BEFORE our handler code runs. So a missing required field, wrong type, etc. bypasses the tool_user_error pattern entirely. Surfaced by live Claude Desktop testing (originally filed as fewd-p0g with wrong framing). Server log line: `WARN serve_inner: rmcp::service: response error id=3 error=ErrorData { code: ErrorCode(-32602), message: "failed to deserialize parameters: missing field source", data: None }`. The LLM called create_recipe without the required source field. ## Design rmcp 1.5 supports the pattern natively — we just need the right primitive: 1. Define `LenientParameters(pub Result)` wrapper. Implement `FromContextPart>` so it NEVER errors at extraction; instead, captures the deserialize Result for the handler to inspect. 2. Convert the 6 tool methods that take real input shapes (search_recipes, get_recipe, list_meals, get_shopping_list, create_recipe, create_meal) to take LenientParameters instead of Parameters. 3. Add explicit `input_schema = rmcp::handler::server::common::schema_for_type::()` to each #[tool] attribute. The macro's `find_parameters_type_in_sig` only matches the literal ident "Parameters", so swapping wrapper types loses schema generation without this override. 4. Each handler matches on the inner Result and returns `Ok(tool_user_error(": . Check the tool schema for required fields."))` on Err. 5. EmptyParams tools (whoami, list_curated_recipes, list_people, get_family_overview) need no conversion — empty schema can't fail deserialize. 6. Wiring test: create_recipe_missing_source_returns_tool_level_error using a JsonObject without the source field; assert tool-level error contains "source" and a recovery hint. ## References - rmcp source: ~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/rmcp-1.5.0/src/handler/server/tool.rs:181-205 (Parameters

+ JsonObject extractors) - rmcp-macros: ~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/rmcp-macros-1.5.0/src/lib.rs:26 (input_schema attribute) and src/common.rs:56-72 (find_parameters_type_in_sig — looks for literal "Parameters" ident) - Existing pattern: server/src/mcp/handler.rs:436-444 (tool_user_error helper)
close_reason: LenientParameters<T> wrapper landed via PR #28 (merge 99d9552). All 10 #[tool] methods now route parameter-deserialize failures through the wrapper to tool_user_error instead of bubbling up as JSON-RPC -32602. The original Claude Desktop failure (LLM omitting required source on create_recipe) now produces an actionable tool-level error: 'create_recipe: missing field source. Check the tool's input schema.' Wrapper API: pub(super) struct with private field, into_tool_input(tool_name) method for the early-return pattern, for_test(value) #[cfg(test)] constructor, static extract(arguments) helper that from_context_part delegates to (testable without constructing #[non_exhaustive] ToolCallContext). EmptyParams tools (whoami, list_curated_recipes, list_people, get_family_overview) wrapped too — currently safe since EmptyParams isn't deny_unknown_fields, but removes the future-hardening trap. Tests: 22 in mcp::handler (3 direct extract tests pin the wrapper layer; the remaining cover handler-side wiring via for_test). Verified: cargo fmt + clippy --all-targets --workspace -- -D warnings + cargo test (165 lib + 92 integration) + cargo build --release all clean. JsonSchema delegation explored and skipped: the rmcp #[tool] macro hardcodes the literal 'Parameters' ident in find_parameters_type_in_sig, so the impl would be dead code unless the explicit input_schema = ... attribute is also present (which it is, on every wrapped tool). DeferredParameters rename also skipped — accurate but not load-bearing.

title: create_recipe duplicate-name behavior: investigate the actual 'Tool execution failed' cause + design choice on auto-dedupe vs explicit MCP rejection
description:
## Surfaced by

Live Claude Desktop testing of PR #27 (fewd-m95). User reported that calling create_recipe with a duplicate name produced an opaque "Tool execution failed" message — the exact JSON-RPC protocol-error pattern the PR was supposed to eliminate.

## Discrepancy: hypothesis vs. code

User's hypothesis (worth checking, but doesn't match the codebase): "If duplicate-name detection in create_recipe is implemented as a SQL UNIQUE constraint that fails at insert time, the resulting error would naturally bubble up as a DB error..."

What the code actually does: server/src/services/recipe_service.rs:97-133 catches `UniqueConstraintViolation` via `is_slug_conflict` and retries with `name-2`, `name-3`, ... up to MAX_SLUG_ATTEMPTS=1000. The current tool description even tells the LLM "The slug is auto-generated from the name (with a numeric suffix on collisions)." So a duplicate name SHOULD succeed silently with a deduped slug, not produce "Tool execution failed".

This means whatever the user observed came from a different code path. Possibilities to investigate with actual server logs:
1. `recipe_to_full(&created, parent_slug_canonical).map_err(internal_error)?` at handler.rs:323 — JSON parse round-trip on stored fields. Would surface as `internal_error` → "Tool execution failed".
2. Some non-UNIQUE DB error during insert (FK violation on parent_recipe_id, NOT NULL on a column we forgot, etc).
3. MAX_SLUG_ATTEMPTS exhaustion (extremely unlikely at 1000).

## Design question (separate from the bug)

Even after the actual root cause is found and patched, there's a UX design choice worth deciding deliberately. Two options:

**Option A: keep auto-dedupe.** Silent "-2 suffix" is invisible to the LLM unless it pays attention to the returned slug. The tool description warns the LLM to search first, but the LLM can still create silent duplicates.

**Option B: reject duplicates at the MCP boundary.** Pre-check via SELECT slug FROM recipes WHERE slug = ? in the create_recipe handler, return tool_user_error("a recipe named 'X' already exists at slug 'reverse-sear'. Use a different name or update the existing recipe.") if found. Service layer keeps auto-dedupe for non-MCP callers (HTTP API). LLM gets an explicit rename-or-update decision.

User preference (from PR #27 feedback): Option B. Quote: "But conceptually, a duplicate name is absolutely recoverable input: the caller can rename and retry. It belongs in the same bucket as unknown-person and unknown-slug."

User also noted the TOCTOU consideration: "There's a TOCTOU window between the check and the insert, but you can wrap both in a transaction if it matters — and for a personal app at this scale, it almost certainly doesn't." Aligns with the fewd-data-migration-posture memory (small user base, design space for clean choices).

## Proposed sequencing

1. Reproduce the original "Tool execution failed" with server logs to find the actual error path (low effort, high value — patches the speculation gap).
2. Land Option B as a separate scoped change: pre-check at MCP boundary, leave service-layer auto-dedupe in place for HTTP. Updates the create_recipe tool description to drop the "-suffix on collisions" line (no longer reachable through MCP).
3. Add wiring test `create_recipe_duplicate_name_returns_tool_level_error` that seeds a recipe and tries to create another with the same name.

## Why not folded into PR #27

The reversed-range bug (fewd-hrc) was a clean extension of the m95 sweep — same validator, same UX class, ~30 lines. This one is two separate problems (root-cause investigation + behavior design choice) that should be reasoned about with logs in hand, not patched speculatively from a hypothesis the code contradicts.
close_reason: Wrong framing — superseded by fewd-sy8, which shipped via PR #28 (merge 99d9552). Original framing was 'create_recipe duplicate-name behavior' based on the user's report that creating a duplicate-name recipe produced 'Tool execution failed'. Live server logs (RUST_LOG=debug session 2026-05-03) showed the actual failure was rmcp's parameter-deserialize layer rejecting calls with missing required fields (-32602 'failed to deserialize parameters: missing field source') — entirely upstream of the duplicate-name code path, which auto-dedupes via RecipeService::create's slug-collision retry loop and was never reached. fewd-sy8 reframed the real category (parameter-deserialize bypass) and shipped the LenientParameters<T> fix. The Option B design discussion (reject duplicates at MCP boundary vs. silent service-layer dedupe) remains open as a separate UX question — file a new bead if/when that's decided. Bead held open through PR review per CLAUDE.md's no-in-PR-closure rule (Copilot caught the violation in PR #28); closing now post-merge per the same convention.

title: DateRangeParams::validate doesn't reject reversed ranges (start_date > end_date) — silent [] from list_meals + get_shopping_list
description:
## Surfaced by

Live Claude Desktop testing of PR #27 (fewd-m95). User feedback: "list_meals and get_shopping_list both returned [] for a reversed date range instead of an error. That's a silent failure rather than a noisy one, which is arguably worse than the opaque error you fixed last round — there's no way for a caller to distinguish 'you queried a backwards range' from 'no meals scheduled.'"

## Root cause

`DateRangeParams::validate` in server/src/mcp/schemas/common.rs:43-47 only checks each date parses as YYYY-MM-DD; it does NOT verify start_date <= end_date. The service layer (server/src/services/meal_service.rs:24-26) is `WHERE date >= start AND date <= end` — when start > end the predicate is unsatisfiable for every row, returning Vec::new(). `get_shopping_list` calls the same path internally, so both tools fail silently in the same way.

This is the same UX class as the unparseable-date bug fewd-m95 fixed for the LLM: an input the LLM can recover from, but only if it gets a signal that something is wrong. Empty results don't signal anything.

## Fix sketch

1. Add `InputError::ReversedDateRange { start_date: String, end_date: String }` to server/src/mcp/schemas/errors.rs with a Display message naming both dates and pointing at the recovery (swap the args).
2. Extend `DateRangeParams::validate` to compare the two parsed `NaiveDate`s and return the new variant when start > end. Equal dates are valid (single-day query).
3. Update `input_error_displays_actionable_messages_for_each_variant` in handler.rs's test mod to cover the new variant.
4. Optional: add a wiring test `list_meals_reversed_date_range_returns_tool_level_error` mirroring the existing `list_meals_invalid_date_returns_tool_level_error`.

The MCP design principle (bd memories fewd-mcp-design-principles, point 1) covers this: error on unknown / invalid references with actionable messages so the LLM can retry.

## Scope decision

Because the bug is closely related to fewd-m95 (same validator, same file, same test mod, same UX class for the LLM) it's a natural fit to fold into PR #27 if not yet merged. If PR #27 has merged, this stands alone as a small follow-up.
close_reason: DateRangeParams::validate now rejects reversed ranges (start_date > end_date) with InputError::ReversedDateRange. Shipped via PR #27 (merge 6358f5f) bundled with fewd-m95. validate_date_yyyy_mm_dd now returns Result<NaiveDate, InputError> so validate() can compare without re-parsing. Both list_meals and get_shopping_list pick up the check automatically through the shared validator. Tests: new variant case in input_error_displays_actionable_messages_for_each_variant, plus list_meals_reversed_date_range_returns_tool_level_error wiring test (skipped get_shopping_list parallel since the routing path is identical and existing date-format tests already prove the wiring on both tools).

title: Sweep MCP tool surface: convert McpError::invalid_params LLM-recoverable errors to CallToolResult::error
description:
Most MCP clients (Claude Desktop, Claude.ai) display JSON-RPC protocol errors (Err(McpError)) as a generic 'Tool execution failed' and DROP the message. Tool-level errors (Ok(CallToolResult { is_error: true, content: [...] })) carry the actionable text through to the LLM so it can retry.

fewd-0kk fixed search_recipes (validate_has_filter rejection AND excludes_for_persons unknown-name path). The same pattern affects every other tool that returns invalid_params for LLM-recoverable input:

- get_recipe — unknown slug (handler.rs ~line 151)
- create_recipe — invalid parent_recipe_slug (~line 240), input validation errors via create_recipe_input_to_dto
- create_meal — unknown person_name / recipe_slug via create_meal_input_to_dto, meal_type validation
- list_meals / get_shopping_list — DateRangeParams::validate failures

Sweep these to use the new tool_user_error helper (or its equivalent) so the actionable messages reach the LLM in clients that don't surface JSON-RPC error messages.

Keep McpError for genuinely internal failures (DB errors, malformed JSON in stored data, missing axum extensions) — those should log server-side and not be LLM-actionable.
close_reason: MCP tool surface fully converted from Err(McpError::invalid_params) to Ok(tool_user_error) for LLM-recoverable input errors. Shipped via PR #27 (merge 6358f5f). Six call sites swept (get_recipe unknown slug, list_meals + get_shopping_list date validation, create_recipe parent_recipe_slug + InputError, create_meal CreateMealError); McpError preserved for genuine internal failures (db_error, internal_error, missing axum extensions, read_resource URI mismatch). CreateMealError match is exhaustive so a future internal-failure variant won't compile-pass without explicit categorization. Eight regression tests pin the contract: five Display-impl tests for the error types, and three call-site wiring tests against in-memory DB. Live Claude Desktop verification confirmed get_recipe rejection ergonomics (points at both list_curated_recipes AND search_recipes for recovery flexibility). Sibling fix fewd-hrc (reversed date range silent failure) bundled into the same PR. Outstanding follow-up fewd-p0g for create_recipe duplicate-name behavior — needs server logs since user's hypothesis (SQL UNIQUE bubbling up) doesn't match the existing auto-dedupe code path.

title: Cooking mode splits one logical step across multiple cards (parseInstructionSteps splits on every \n)
description:
Surfaced by user testing on the deployed dietpi instance (2026-04-29). In cooking mode, a single logical instruction step is rendered as 3-6 separate numbered cards. Screenshot example (Bolognese recipe, AI-enhanced instructions):

  Card 1: 'Heat 4 tbsp olive oil in a large heavy pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add onion,'
  Card 2: 'carrot, and celery. Cook, stirring occasionally, until very soft and starting'
  Card 3: 'to turn golden — about 15 minutes. Don'\''t rush this.'
  Card 4: 'Add garlic and cook 1 minute more.'
  Card 5: 'Increase heat to medium-high. Add ground beef and pork in chunks. Break up'
  Card 6: 'and brown thoroughly. Season generously with salt and pepper.'

Cards 1-3 should be ONE step. Card 4 is correctly its own step. Cards 5-6 should be ONE step.

Root cause: src/types/recipe.ts:219-224

    export function parseInstructionSteps(instructions: string): string[] {
      return instructions
        .split('\n')
        .map((line) => line.replace(/^\s*\d+[.)]\s*/, '').trim())
        .filter((line) => line.length > 0)
    }

The function splits on every '\n', but the AI-enhanced instructions (from useEnhancedInstructions, see CookingView.tsx:54-58) contain hard-wrapped lines within a single paragraph. Every soft-wrap becomes a 'step'.

The non-enhanced path (parsed.instructions from the markdown parser) may or may not exhibit this — depends on whether the source markdown has soft-wrapped lines. The bug bites hardest on AI-enhanced output because LLMs tend to hard-wrap at ~80 chars.

Fix: split on paragraph breaks (\n\n+) instead of single \n. If the instructions are a numbered list, split on the leading number markers (^\s*\d+[.)]\s*) so a single step that wraps across multiple lines stays whole. The existing test at src/types/recipe.test.ts:162 ('1. Boil water.\n2. Add pasta.\n3) Stir.') should still pass.

Test cases to add:
1. Hard-wrapped paragraph: 'Heat oil in pan.\nAdd onions.\nCook until soft.' is currently TREATED as 3 steps but the user-intended split depends on whether the source has blank-line separation. Add fixtures based on actual AI-enhanced output (capture from useEnhancedInstructions for the Bolognese recipe).
2. Numbered list with internal wrapping: '1. Heat oil.\n   Add onions.\n2. Add garlic.' → 2 steps, not 3.
3. Mixed paragraph + numbered list (edge case from real data).

Touchpoints:
- src/types/recipe.ts (parseInstructionSteps)
- src/types/recipe.test.ts (new test cases for soft-wrap paragraphs and numbered lists with internal wrapping)
- src/components/CookingView.test.tsx (integration coverage with enhanced + non-enhanced paths)

This affects every recipe rendered in cooking mode with enhanced instructions, so user impact is broad — bumping to P2.
close_reason: Closed

title: scripts/ci-check.sh is broken — contains Unicode smart quotes
description:
scripts/ci-check.sh fails to run with `command not found` errors because
the file contains Unicode typographical characters instead of ASCII shell
metacharacters:

  - U+201C / U+201D (curly double quotes "" "")  in place of "

Confirm with hexdump:

title: Consolidate workspace deps and remove stale server/Cargo.lock
description:
## Why
Two issues caused duplicate Dependabot PRs (e.g. #11/#12 for rand, #13/#14 for rustls-webpki):

1. **Stale `server/Cargo.lock`** — leftover from before the workspace conversion. Cargo only reads the root `/Cargo.lock` (workspace resolves all members at root), so this file is dead weight Dependabot scans independently.
2. **No `[workspace.dependencies]`** — direct deps are declared independently in each member crate, so updating shared deps requires touching multiple files.

## What's needed
- Delete `/server/Cargo.lock`
- Add `[workspace.package]` for shared metadata (edition, version)
- Add `[workspace.dependencies]` for cross-member shared deps (`tokio`) and ecosystem-pinned families (`sea-orm` + `sea-orm-migration` must stay in lockstep)
- Update `server/Cargo.toml` and `server/migration/Cargo.toml` to inherit via `workspace = true`
- Verify `cargo build --release` and `cargo test` still clean

## Scope
Pre-req for the v2026-04-24.1 hotfix release. Branch + PR (per repo convention for production-touching changes).
notes: Implementation complete on branch chore/workspace-deps-consolidation. Verified: workspace cargo check, cargo test (17 migration tests pass), cargo build --release (no feature-flag drift), cargo fmt/clippy clean. Root Cargo.lock unchanged — pure refactor. Ready for PR.
close_reason: Merged via PR #16 (commit 91028c7). Removed stale server/Cargo.lock and consolidated tokio + sea-orm + sea-orm-migration into [workspace.dependencies]. Future Dependabot PRs should no longer duplicate per-lockfile.

title: Add CI smoke-test for migration drift (run against pre-existing schema snapshot)
description:
## Why
fewd-???-recipe-slug-fix discovered that CI cannot detect when an already-applied migration is edited in place (which silently breaks any DB that ran the original version). CI builds always start from an empty DB, so the modified migration runs from scratch and works. Production DBs that already ran the original don't get the schema change.

## What's needed
Add a CI step (or test) that:
1. Restores a checked-in SQLite snapshot of an older schema state (e.g. one captured at each release tag)
2. Boots the server / runs migrations against it
3. Asserts the schema matches what current code expects (e.g. by running representative queries: list recipes, list drink_recipes, list meals)
4. Fails CI if a query 500s on the migrated old DB

## Implementation sketch
- Add \`server/test-fixtures/schema-snapshots/v2026-04-24.db\` (or similar — capture per release)
- Add an integration test under \`server/tests/migration_compat.rs\` that opens the snapshot, runs migrations, executes representative queries
- Update \`just ci\` and \`.github/workflows/ci.yml\` to run it

## Risks
- Snapshot maintenance: a snapshot per release tag is the cleanest contract but adds a manual step (or could be automated via a release hook)
- Binary diffs in git are noisy — consider committing the snapshot as a SQL dump (\`.sql\` text) and rebuilding the DB from it at test time

## Scope decision
Single PR after the slug-fix lands. Snapshot strategy decision is the design call worth deferring until we look at file sizes.
notes: Implementation in PR #18. Awaiting CI to confirm release build + smoke test step pass on macos-latest. Locally verified: happy path green, deliberate corruption (slug column stripped) produces curl 22 / HTTP 500 from /api/recipes and /api/drink-recipes with full server log dumped, exit 1.
close_reason: Closed

title: Split IngredientDto.name into name + prep (purchase form vs. preparation form)
description:
Today IngredientDto.name bundles the purchasable thing and the preparation state into one string ('garlic cloves, thinly sliced', 'lemon, cut into wedges for serving'). Two downstream problems:

1. Shopping-list readability: the list surfaces prep state as if it's what you buy. Nobody buys pre-sliced garlic.

2. Aggregation can't collapse across recipes: three recipes with 'garlic, minced', 'garlic cloves, thinly sliced', and 'whole garlic cloves' read as three different ingredients and produce three shopping-list lines instead of one.

Claude (MCP consumer) flagged both when preparing a real grocery list.

Data-model change:

    pub struct IngredientDto {
        pub name: String,           // 'garlic'       — the thing you buy
        pub prep: Option<String>,   // 'thinly sliced' — how the recipe uses it
        pub amount: IngredientAmountDto,
        pub unit: Unit,              // see fewd-lm3
        pub notes: Option<String>,
    }

Recipe instructions/UI compose display as 'name, prep' where prep is present. Shopping list aggregates by name alone.

**Scope**:

1. Add the field everywhere IngredientDto appears: dto.rs, MCP IngredientOut in schemas/common.rs, CreateRecipeInput, recipe-edit UI form, cooking-mode display, URL-import recipe parser, shopping aggregator.

2. **Migration**: per fewd-data-migration-posture memory, don't hedge on existing rows. One-shot migration walks every recipe, runs each ingredient name through either (a) an LLM classifier (Claude API call given the ingredient, returns structured name + prep) or (b) a rule-based splitter keyed on 'name, prep-verb' patterns like 'X, minced' / 'X, thinly sliced' / 'X, cut into Y'. Dry-run the migration, spot-check a handful, then commit. For recipes where the split is ambiguous, leave prep=None and the name unchanged as an escape hatch.

3. Shopping aggregator: group by name (case-insensitive) ignoring prep. Interacts mildly with fewd-wm6 (staples classification) since the classifier keys on name — a split name is cleaner to classify on.

**Edge case to handle during migration**: 'boneless skinless chicken breast' vs 'whole chicken' are the same name but different purchases. Naive 'aggregate by name' is wrong here. Options: (a) treat name strings as already distinguishing ('chicken breast' vs 'whole chicken' are different names, period), (b) add a purchase_form field as a third axis, (c) accept occasional mis-aggregation. Lean (a) — simplest, and the ambiguity surfaces naturally in the LLM / rule splitter.
acceptance_criteria: IngredientDto has split name + Option<String> prep. All consumers (Recipe edit UI, cooking mode, MCP schemas, shopping aggregator, URL parser) handle the new shape. One-shot migration re-splits existing recipes via LLM-assisted or rule-based classifier, with a dry-run + spot-check step before commit. Shopping aggregation collapses prep variants of the same name into one line. Edge case of 'chicken breast' vs 'whole chicken' handled (chose strategy (a): distinct names = distinct purchases).
notes:
Implemented across 7 commits on branch fewd-xez/split-ingredient-name-and-prep:

ca22130 add IngredientDto.prep field with no behavior change
07ebf3b paren-aware ingredient name/prep splitter + 9 unit tests
36b71b2 wire splitter into recipe_parser, MCP ingredient_in, recipe_import_service (prompt + defensive pass)
2e668ec backfill migration m20260427_000013 walking only the recipes table (drinks + adhoc are empty per prod audit)
23f1e71 frontend prep field + formatIngredientLabel display rule across 7 components
92c15f1 end-to-end shopping aggregation tests + strategy-A guard
dca9f03 cargo fmt pass

Quality gates: cargo fmt --check ✓, cargo clippy --all-targets --workspace -- -D warnings ✓, cargo test --workspace (96+67+32 passed) ✓, bun run test (298 passed) ✓, bun run lint ✓, dprint check ✓, cargo build --release ✓.

Live calibration: splitter unit-tested against the actual 42 clean-split prod ingredient strings dumped from dietpi on 2026-04-27. Migration tested against synthesized DBs with comma'd, paren-bearing, already-split, no-comma, and mixed-recipe rows.

Acceptance verification: backend tests prove the load-bearing 'two recipes with different prep aggregate to one shopping line' invariant. Local dev-server live verification deferred — port 3000 is occupied by a long-running dev session; user can restart to see migration apply on dev DB. Migration tests cover the same logic against in-memory DBs. dietpi deploy is the production-equivalent verification per CLAUDE.md.

Out of scope (filed as fewd-4i3): pre-existing parser bugs surfaced by the audit — em-dash ranges, Unicode fractions, compound units that splitn(3) mis-buckets.

title: Shopping list: classify + separate pantry staples (don't filter, split)
description:
Pantry staples — kosher salt, black pepper, olive oil, garlic powder, smoked paprika, red pepper flakes, etc. — appear in the shopping list today as line items indistinguishable from real shopping needs. They're noise unless the user is actually out of them, and the server can't know that.

Right shape, based on live Claude feedback: DON'T filter them out. Return them in a separate section so consumers (LLM or UI) can present 'stuff to buy' and 'stuff to double-check' distinctly. A shopping list that says 'buy these 8 items; also verify the smoked paprika' is more useful than one that silently drops the staple — especially for an LLM that can phrase the verification naturally in conversation.

Response shape:

    {
      "items_to_buy": [...],
      "pantry_staples_to_verify": [...]
    }

Classification approach: COMPUTED at list-generation time, not stored per-ingredient. A self-contained classifier module taking (ingredient_name, unit, total_amount) → bool. Rules:

1. Small-measurement units (tsp, tbsp, pinch, dash) → staple. These units almost universally indicate a spice or seasoning that you buy in a jar and use sparingly.

2. Name-based allowlist for units where the unit alone isn't diagnostic: salt, pepper, kosher salt, black pepper, olive oil, avocado oil, vegetable oil, butter (small amounts), flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, vinegar (small amounts), common spices (cumin, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, chili powder, oregano, thyme, basil, bay leaves, etc). Document the list; expand as false negatives surface.

Why not stored per-ingredient: would require every recipe author (human or LLM) to classify, plus UI affordances, plus a migration. The accuracy gain over heuristics is modest for a household app. If false positives become a problem ('this recipe genuinely calls for salt as a key ingredient'), add an optional per-ingredient override later — the heuristic stays the default.

Connects to fewd-kif, which exposes the two-section response through MCP and UI.
acceptance_criteria: ShoppingService returns a structured response with items_to_buy and pantry_staples_to_verify as separate arrays. The staple classifier is a standalone function with clear rules, covered by unit tests for each category (small-measurement units, allowlisted names, legitimate non-staples that must NOT be classified as staple). Allowlist documented in the source. Works on both the raw aggregated amounts and the rounded amounts from fewd-p3j.
notes: Preserve these existing-behavior invariants when touching ShoppingService output (called out by live Claude Desktop consumer as the tool's strongest properties): (1) per-ingredient source breakdown — each aggregated item carries a list of contributing (meal_id, date, meal_type, recipe_name, amount) so the consumer can answer 'why is there extra flour?'; (2) aggregation shape is total + sources, not total OR sources — keep both; (3) range math preserves Range { min, max } through scaling, doesn't collapse to Single on convenient simplification.

title: Shopping list: round up to grocery-realistic amounts (counts + weights + volumes)
description:
The current shopping list returns mathematically exact scaled amounts — 1.75 lb potatoes, 0.88 lemons, 0.875 pinch red pepper flakes. Nobody shops in those quantities. Introduce a 'shopping amounts' view that rounds up each aggregated ingredient to something you'd actually buy.

Rules in order of trivial-to-heuristic:

1. Count-unit ingredients (each, whole, head, clove, bunch): ceil to the next whole integer. 0.88 lemons → 1, 2.4 heads garlic → 3.

2. Weight units (lb, oz, g, kg) and volume units with grocery equivalents (cup, quart, gallon, liter): round up using a sliding scale. Small amounts (< 0.5 unit) → nearest 0.25; medium (< 2 units) → nearest 0.5; large (≥ 2 units) → nearest 1. So 1.75 lb → 2 lb, 0.3 cup → 0.5 cup, 4.2 lb → 5 lb.

3. Small-measurement units (tsp, tbsp, pinch, dash): tracked separately (see the pantry-staples bead) since these are almost always things you already own.

Implementation: new service-layer function, e.g. ShoppingService::get_shopping_list_rounded(start, end) or ShoppingService::get_shopping_list(start, end, format: ShoppingFormat) where ShoppingFormat has variants Recipe (current behavior) and Shopping (the rounded version). Returns a GroceryListItem DTO with display_amount: String (e.g. '2 lb'), display_unit: String, raw_amount: Option<IngredientAmountDto> for secondary display, and whatever_round_occurred flags for UI hints.

Unit-conversion logic belongs in the existing unit_converter module. Rounding tables and category classification (count vs weight vs small-measurement) can live alongside.

Integration is a follow-up bead.
acceptance_criteria: New function in ShoppingService returns rounded GroceryListItem values. Count units always ceil to integers. Weight/volume units follow the sliding rounding scale. Small-measurement units passed through as-is (filter work happens in the pantry bead). Unit tests cover each ingredient-category rule with edge values (exact round numbers, just-below thresholds, very small, very large).
notes: Preserve these existing-behavior invariants when touching ShoppingService output (called out by live Claude Desktop consumer as the tool's strongest properties): (1) per-ingredient source breakdown — each aggregated item carries a list of contributing (meal_id, date, meal_type, recipe_name, amount) so the consumer can answer 'why is there extra flour?'; (2) aggregation shape is total + sources, not total OR sources — keep both; (3) range math preserves Range { min, max } through scaling, doesn't collapse to Single on convenient simplification.

title: Recipe discovery redesign: list_curated_recipes + search_recipes with persona filters
description:
Two concerns at 150+ recipe scale: unfiltered dumps are a context tax (~8-15k tokens per call), and there's no direct way for the LLM to filter against family members' dislikes without pulling every recipe's ingredients and cross-checking in-conversation.

Design:

1. RENAME list_recipes → list_curated_recipes. No params. Returns a bounded ~30-item shortlist (favorites + recently-made + top-rated, de-duped). Name makes clear this is a selection, not an enumeration.

2. EXPAND search_recipes. Required: at least one non-trivial filter (empty / query='*' both rejected with pointer to list_curated_recipes). Filters:
   - query (current substring on name)
   - tags: Vec<String>
   - max_total_time_minutes: i32
   - min_rating: f64
   - is_favorite: bool
   - unmade_since_days: i32
   - excludes_for_persons: Vec<String> — reject any recipe whose ingredient NAMES contain any of the listed active persons' dislikes (simple case-insensitive substring; explicitly document that 'olive oil' is rejected when 'olive' is disliked so the LLM can plan around false positives)

3. NOT in this pass: favorites-based matching (ranking problem, not filter), dietary-goals matching (free-form text, needs LLM judgment), pagination (shortlist is bounded, search is filter-bounded).

Full-archive dump intentionally not exposed — not an LLM use case; web UI is there for humans who want to scroll everything.

Implementation: push all filters into the SeaORM query, not post-filtering in Rust, so it scales with catalog size.
acceptance_criteria: list_curated_recipes returns ≤30 blended favorites/recent/top-rated with documented policy. search_recipes rejects bare calls with a helpful error. excludes_for_persons resolves names via the existing MealLookups pattern, loads each person's dislikes, and filters at the DB layer (LIKE / LOWER matches on ingredient names). Docs call out the substring-match caveats. No tool returns the full archive.
close_reason: Recipe discovery redesign shipped via PR #26 (merge ee8b40b). list_curated_recipes (≤30 favorites + recent + top-rated, slug-sorted, dedup'd) and search_recipes (composable filters: query, tags, max_total_time_minutes, min_rating, is_favorite, unmade_since_days, excludes_for_persons) are live on the MCP surface. Tool-level errors via CallToolResult{is_error:true} so messages reach the LLM. Follow-ups: fewd-2fc (normalize total_time → total_minutes), fewd-m95 (sweep remaining MCP tools to use tool_user_error), fewd-0a9 (optional sort_by parameter).

title: Scrub pre-d92 family PII from git history
description:
After fewd-d92 removes hardcoded family names from HEAD, the real names (Steve/Amanda/Vivienne/Cleo + real birthdates) still exist in every historical commit that touched server/src/services/seed_data.rs — back through the initial commit. The Person-entity example in REQUIREMENTS.md has the same issue. Scrub these from history via git filter-repo, then force-push main.

Pre-conditions confirmed by owner (2026-04-21):
- Repo has been public only a few days.
- No known external clones or collaborators.
- Accepts that GitHub's ~90-day cached commit views will expire naturally; no GitHub Support ticket needed.
- Accepts that the fork at turboladen/fewd (source of PR #9) will have divergent history; coordinate ad-hoc if needed.

Approach sketch:
- Install git filter-repo (Homebrew).
- Use --replace-text with a substitutions file covering the four real first names and the four real birthdates, mapping each to its fewd-d92 placeholder equivalent so old commits become compilable.
- Verify locally: fresh clone of the rewritten repo, cargo build across a sample of historical SHAs.
- Force-push main. Do NOT touch refs/dolt/data (beads state is independent).
- Post-push: delete local .git/refs/original/, re-clone to confirm, update any bd memory entries that reference pre-rewrite SHAs.

title: Cooking mode: ADHD-friendly enhancements (step check-off, current-step highlight, ingredient check-off)
description:
Builds on fewd-pqb (the calm focused view). After shipping the base cooking mode and using it in the kitchen a few times, add interaction features that help cooks (especially those with ADHD) stay anchored to where they are in the recipe.

Scope:
- Tap a step card to mark it complete (fades to ~50% opacity, number gets a soft strikethrough or subtle dim)
- Tap an ingredient to mark it as added (line-through style)
- Visual highlight on the 'current' step (the topmost not-yet-completed step) — gentle terracotta border or background tint
- Optional: persist progress per-recipe in localStorage so reloading or briefly leaving doesn't wipe place
- All state local — no server persistence

Why higher priority than multi-recipe selection:
- Daily impact for the actual kitchen user
- The base CookingView component should be designed to absorb these features; doing them next while the design context is fresh keeps the architecture clean

Acceptance:
- Tapping a step toggles its completed state visually
- Tapping an ingredient toggles its 'added' state visually
- Current step (first incomplete) is visually distinct
- Reloading mid-cook restores progress (if persistence is included)
- Exiting cooking mode and re-entering: TBD — discuss whether progress should reset (likely yes for first-cut)
- Existing cooking-mode behavior (chrome hidden, wake lock, escape/exit) is preserved

title: Cover ErrorBoundary with tests
description: ErrorBoundary prevents one bad component from white-screening the entire app. Currently untested — a regression would only surface when a real production error fires. Small scope, high blast radius if broken.
acceptance_criteria:

title: MCP: route authenticated_name() failures through tracing
description:

- Line 461: \"missing authenticated person\"

title: MCP: enforce AuthenticatedPerson via typed extractor (or delete)
description:
AuthenticatedPerson is plumbed end-to-end via request extensions (server/src/mcp/mod.rs auth middleware) but only one tool (whoami) reads it. create_meal, create_recipe, and every other write tool ignore the authenticated identity entirely.

Today this is 'by design' (any-authed-user-is-admin, documented in fewd-2y6.3). The structural problem is that the extension exists, is plumbed everywhere, and is unused on the write path. A future contributor who adds a 'self-only' authorization check will probably add it to one tool and miss the others — there's no enforcement.

**Fix options:**
1. Wrap AuthenticatedPerson in a typed extractor that every tool function takes by parameter — type system enforces 'authenticated context is plumbed everywhere.' Add a single integration test that calls each write tool and asserts the authenticated context was visible.
2. Delete AuthenticatedPerson and document the model as 'no per-user state at all.'

Option 1 keeps the door open for future authorization work. Option 2 removes a footgun.

NOT release-gating — file for follow-up.

title: MCP: tighten CORS scope — drop Authorization from allowlist or skip CORS for /mcp
description:
CORS allowlist (server/src/main.rs:33-53) is hard-coded to localhost:5173/3000/3001 and includes Authorization and mcp-session-id in AllowHeaders. Combined with the low-entropy name-bearer auth, an attacker who plants a malicious page that the user visits while running fewd locally could enumerate names and cross-origin POST tool calls. tower_http::cors::CorsLayer defaults to allow_credentials(false), so cookies don't ride along, but the attacker's JS could still send arbitrary Authorization headers.

**Fix options:**
1. Drop Authorization from the CORS Allow-Headers list (browsers can't call /mcp at all from a non-same-origin page).
2. Skip CORS entirely for /mcp — apply the layer only to the SPA-serving routes. mcp-remote and Claude Desktop don't need CORS.

Option 2 is cleaner if /mcp is never called from a browser context.

NOT release-gating — defense-in-depth concern stacked on the already-documented LAN-only posture.

title: Shopping aggregator: UX decision for or_alternative ingredients
description:
Follow-up to fewd-4nb (parser support for 'or N alt' alternatives).

Per the open question filed in fewd-4nb's comments: when a recipe row carries
`{ primary: 8 flour tortillas, or_alternative: 10 corn tortillas }`,
what does the shopping aggregator do?

## Options

(a) **Count primary only.** Simple. But: shopper picks the alternative at cook time and the list is wrong.
(b) **Count both.** Safe (you have both), but doubles the buy and the alternative is the *substitute*, not an addition.
(c) **Per-meal user choice in UI.** Toggle primary-or-alternative at meal-add time; aggregator counts whichever is selected. Most flexible, most UI work.
(d) **Surface as 'either/or' on the list.** Aggregator counts primary in the consolidated section and lists the alternative separately as 'or N corn tortillas (substitute for flour-tortillas line)'. Hybrid.

## State today (post-fewd-4nb)

- IngredientDto carries `or_alternative` end-to-end through parsing and shopping_service rebuild.
- Aggregator (shopping_service.rs:~123) groups by primary `name` only — current behavior matches option (a) by default.
- The data is preserved on the IngredientDto, so any of the four options can be implemented without re-touching the parser or DTO.

## Decision driver

The right answer probably depends on whether substitution is a planning-time
or shopping-time choice in the user's mental model. (a) and (c) imply the
same data shape (just a flag/state); (d) wants the list-rendering layer to
know about the relationship structurally.

## Touchpoints when implementing

- server/src/services/shopping_service.rs (aggregation + scaled rebuild)
- src/components/ShoppingList.tsx (rendering)
- src/components/MealPlanner.tsx (per-meal toggle, if option c)

title: Treat ingredient size/grade qualifiers as first-class attributes for shopping consolidation
description:
## Insight

Words like `medium`, `large`, `small`, `extra-large`, `jumbo` before an ingredient name aren't purely descriptive — they affect whether two recipes' ingredient rows should merge on the shopping list.

Example: Recipe A calls for `8 medium flour tortillas`, Recipe B calls for `6 large flour tortillas`. Today the parser keeps `medium` / `large` inside `name` (per the fewd-4i3 compound-name path), and the shopping aggregator keys on `name.to_lowercase()` (per `ingredient_splitter.rs:9-11`). Result: two unrelated rows on the shopping list — `medium flour tortillas: 8` and `large flour tortillas: 6` — with no UI affordance for the shopper to either:

- Consolidate to one size (buy 14 large, skip medium) — common in real cooking; sizes are usually substitutable
- Buy both as listed
- See that they describe the same purchasable thing

The chef's mental model: "size matters for the recipe, but at purchase time I'll often pick one." The data model needs to expose that choice rather than burying the relationship.

## Direction

Extract size/grade qualifiers into a separate field on `IngredientDto`:

    size_qualifier: Option<String>  // "medium", "large", etc.

Or a structured enum if the qualifier vocabulary is closed enough. Ingredient name then carries only the purchasable noun (`flour tortillas`).

Shopping aggregator changes:
- Primary key: `name.to_lowercase()` (unchanged shape; what's in `name` is now narrower)
- Within a key, group entries by `size_qualifier`
- UI surfaces the size variation as an explicit consolidation prompt or a multi-line entry

## Open questions

1. **Vocabulary scope.** Is this just size (`small`/`medium`/`large`/`xl`/`jumbo`) or does it also cover grade (`extra-virgin`, `kosher`, `unsalted`)? They feel like the same axis to me — both are "qualities of the canonical ingredient that the shopper might consolidate or keep distinct" — but they parse differently in source text and may want separate fields.
2. **Varietal modifiers.** `Asian pear`, `Roma tomato`, `kabocha squash` — these are species/cultivar, not qualifiers. They're likely a *different* field (`variety`?) since substituting cultivars changes the dish more than substituting sizes. Out of scope for this bead unless it's cheaper to design them together.
3. **Migration story.** Existing rows have qualifiers baked into `name`. A backfill migration would need to extract them — sibling pattern to `m20260427_000013_split_ingredient_name_and_prep` and `m20260428_000014_reparse_misbucketed_ingredients`. Same canonical-helper approach: shared parser in the migration crate, server re-exports.

## Related

- fewd-4nb — `or_alternative` field (sibling parser/data-model change; size qualifier could land first or second, no hard ordering)
- fewd-4i3 — current "medium → compound name" behavior is exactly what this would walk back, intentionally (the trade-off there was "preserve descriptors at the cost of weird names"; this gives us both)
- `server/src/services/ingredient_splitter.rs` — splitter precedent for shared name/prep extraction
- Conversation 2026-05-03 surfaced this when tracing `8 medium flour tortillas (8-inch) or 10 corn tortillas` through the parser

## Acceptance (to refine before implementation)

- `IngredientDto` has `size_qualifier: Option<String>`
- Parser extracts a closed vocabulary of size words (start small: `small`, `medium`, `large`, `extra-large`, `xl`, `jumbo`) when they appear before the noun
- Backfill migration repairs existing rows
- Shopping aggregator groups by `(name, size_qualifier)` but surfaces variations to the UI in a way that supports consolidation choice (UI design out of scope for this bead — just expose the data shape)

title: Parser: support 'or N <alt>' ingredient alternatives via or_alternative field
description:
## Problem

The recipe markdown parser silently flattens lines like:

    * 8 medium flour tortillas (8-inch) or 10 corn tortillas

Into a single `IngredientDto` with `name="medium flour tortillas (8-inch) or 10 corn tortillas"`, amount=8, unit="whole". The "or 10 corn tortillas" alternative is lost — buried in the name field, so:

- It cannot be selected/swapped in the UI
- It will never collapse with a clean `corn tortillas` shopping-list key (aggregator keys on `name.to_lowercase()` per `ingredient_splitter.rs:9-11`)
- The row has its own unique permanent key, divorced from both `flour tortillas` and `corn tortillas`

The parser produces no error — silent success, which is exactly the failure mode `live_data_calibration` tests exist to surface.

## Decision

Option C: add `or_alternative: Option<Box<IngredientDto>>` to `IngredientDto`. Recursive (alternative carries its own amount/unit/prep/notes). One field, no list — most recipe lines have at most one "or" alternative.

Picked over (a) free-text notes (loses structure) and (b) sibling DTO with flag (changes call-site iteration semantics in shopping aggregator + UI).

## Scope

1. `server/src/dto.rs`: add `or_alternative: Option<Box<IngredientDto>>` to `IngredientDto`. Mirror in any DB-backed entity if ingredients are stored structurally (check `entities/recipe_ingredient.rs` or wherever the JSON column lives — likely just JSON text storage, in which case no migration needed; verify before assuming).
2. `server/src/services/recipe_parser.rs`: detect ` or ` at depth 0 in the name segment after `peel_size_paren` and `extract_notes` have run. Split, recursively parse the right half as a fresh ingredient line. Care: do not split inside parens (depth-aware, like `first_top_level_comma`). Only split when the right half has the shape `<amount> <name>` — bare `or` clauses inside compound names ("salt or pepper to taste") should NOT split.
3. `src/types/`: mirror in TypeScript — `orAlternative?: Ingredient`.
4. UI: decide rendering (collapsed by default with toggle? "8 flour tortillas (or 10 corn tortillas)" inline?). Out of scope for this bead — file a follow-up once parser + types land.
5. Shopping aggregator: define behavior. Default: count only the primary, ignore alternatives. Discuss before implementing.

## Acceptance

- `* 8 medium flour tortillas (8-inch) or 10 corn tortillas` parses to:
  - primary: name="flour tortillas", amount=8, unit="whole", notes=Some("8-inch") (or "medium flour tortillas" — depends on `medium` handling, which is the existing fewd-4i3 trade-off)
  - or_alternative: Some({ name="corn tortillas", amount=10, unit="whole" })
- `* salt or pepper to taste` does NOT split (no parseable amount on right half).
- `* 1 cup milk (or 1 cup half-and-half)` continues to work as before — the parens-with-unit-token case is owned by `peel_size_paren`, not the new `or` splitter.
- Add a `live_data_calibration` entry covering the tortillas line and at least one negative case.

## References

- `server/src/services/recipe_parser.rs:175` — `parse_ingredient_line`
- `server/src/services/ingredient_splitter.rs:34` — `first_top_level_comma` (template for depth-aware splitting)
- `server/migration/src/paren_notes.rs` — sibling peeler precedent
- Conversation 2026-05-03 traced the actual parser output empirically before filing this
close_reason: Closed

title: MCP search_recipes: optional sort_by parameter (name | rating | last_made | most_made)
description:
Today both list_curated_recipes and search_recipes return results in a fixed order: get_curated blends favorites + recent + top-rated, and search_recipes orders by slug ASC (deterministic but not always what the LLM wants).

Real-world LLM use cases would benefit from explicit sort control:

- 'show me my highest-rated dinners' — sort by rating DESC
- 'what haven't we made in a while?' — sort by last_made ASC NULLS FIRST (or by unmade_since_days as a filter, which we already have, but the *ordering* of the result still defaults to slug)
- 'most-made recipes this year' — sort by times_made DESC

Proposed:

  sort_by: Option<RecipeSortField>  (Name | Slug | Rating | LastMade | TimesMade | CreatedAt)
  sort_order: Option<SortOrder>     (Asc | Desc, default depends on field)

If left None, current slug-ASC default applies. Document defaults in the tool description so the LLM doesn't need to guess.

Discovered while iterating on Claude Chat feedback for fewd-0kk: the user noticed that 'garlicky potatoes' (lowercased name) sorted after 'Thai Green Curry' under SQLite's BINARY collation; switching to slug-ASC fixed the immediate determinism problem but the broader UX is 'callers should be able to ask for the order they want.'
